summary_hint: <recipient_name> receives <ordered_amount>/<payment_frequency> alimony/spousal support from <payer_name> under <court_or_agreement_type> dated <order_or_agreement_date>; status <current_payment_status>, order runs through <end_date_or_termination_events>.

typed_core.name: document_title
typed_core.why: identity / disambiguator: distinguishes a court order vs a separation agreement vs a third-party verification letter — each treated differently for income durability

typed_core.name: issuer_name
typed_core.why: identity / processor: who produced the verification (court, attorney, SDU) — third-party independence check

typed_core.name: recipient_name
typed_core.why: identity: whose income this is; matches the support recipient to the borrower

typed_core.name: payer_name
typed_core.why: identity: the obligor; party matching and to confirm the recipient is not also the payer

typed_core.name: court_or_agreement_type
typed_core.why: identity/disambiguator: the legal basis (court order vs voluntary agreement) drives whether the income is acceptable

typed_core.name: court_name
typed_core.why: identity: the issuing court; provenance of the order

typed_core.name: case_number
typed_core.why: identity / dedup: the case key that ties this to other filings for the same borrower

typed_core.name: order_or_agreement_date
typed_core.why: identity/disambiguator: which order governs; distinguishes the original from a later modification

typed_core.name: modification_date
typed_core.why: disambiguator for order_or_agreement_date: when the terms were last changed — the governing amount may be the modified one

typed_core.name: support_type
typed_core.why: disambiguator: alimony vs child support vs separate maintenance — child support has different continuance/gross-up treatment; misreading inverts the income analysis
typed_core.prompt_hint: Distinguish alimony/spousal support from child support explicitly — do not collapse them; keep support_type verbatim

typed_core.name: ordered_amount
typed_core.why: processor: the periodic support amount — the headline income figure

typed_core.name: payment_frequency
typed_core.why: disambiguator for ordered_amount: monthly vs biweekly vs weekly changes the annualized income; the amount is uninterpretable without it
typed_core.prompt_hint: Report the payment frequency alongside the amount, verbatim, even when the annual figure is also stated

typed_core.name: start_date
typed_core.why: processor: when receipt began — bounds the receipt-history window an underwriter reviews

typed_core.name: end_date_or_termination_events
typed_core.why: processor: continuance — support must be expected to continue ~3 years to count; captures fixed end date or trigger events (remarriage, emancipation)
typed_core.prompt_hint: Capture continuance: the fixed end date OR the termination trigger events — do not compute the ~3-year test

typed_core.name: escalation_or_cost_of_living_terms
typed_core.why: processor / disambiguator: future amount changes (COLA) that make ordered_amount a floor, not the final figure

typed_core.name: arrears_balance
typed_core.why: processor: an arrears balance signals unreliable receipt — directly affects whether the income is counted
typed_core.prompt_hint: Capture arrears faithfully — describes receipt reliability; do NOT judge whether the income counts

typed_core.name: current_payment_status
typed_core.why: processor: current/delinquent/paid — the single strongest receipt-reliability signal

typed_core.name: third_party_collection_or_sdu
typed_core.why: processor: a State Disbursement Unit / third-party collector produces documented, verifiable receipt — strengthens the income

typed_core.name: deposit_account_last4
typed_core.why: PII (restricted, last-4): the account support is deposited to; matches the income to a verified bank deposit
typed_core.prompt_hint: Last-4 of a deposit account is PII even though partial — file it here, never the catch-all

typed_core.name: document_issue_date
typed_core.why: processor: verification age / recency — a stale verification may need refresh

typed_core.name: loan_number
typed_core.why: identity: links the document to the loan file (confidential)

nested_lists.name: payment_history
nested_lists.shape_reason: a support-payment history genuinely repeats (typically 12-24 monthly rows), and per-field wrapping would risk the 16,384-token ceiling for a long history — flat rows are the light shape

fields.name: amount
fields.why: the payment amount — supports the stable-receipt analysis
fields.pii_note: payment-history rows may carry an account reference; the nested record needs its own redactor if any account digits appear (the transaction-description pattern)

rejected.name: form_number, form_revision_date
rejected.reason: not a standardized form; a court order / agreement is free-form

rejected.name: issuer_address, issuer_phone, issuer_email_or_url
rejected.reason: contact detail with no consumer; catch-all captures it if needed

rejected.name: effective_date, expiration_date, statement_period_start, statement_period_end
rejected.reason: duplicate start_date / order_or_agreement_date; the document has no coverage period

rejected.name: party_names, party_addresses
rejected.reason: redundant — the relevant parties are recipient_name and payer_name

rejected.name: property_address
rejected.reason: not present on a support order/verification

rejected.name: account_case_reference_number
rejected.reason: duplicates case_number flattened from the court object

rejected.name: signature_blocks, notary_block
rejected.reason: execution/notarization not consumed by any rule; the order's authority is the court, not a signature

rejected.name: document_status_or_version
rejected.reason: low value; modification_date already captures the amendment signal

rejected.name: expected_continuance_months
rejected.reason: a derived conclusion (computed from end_date_or_termination_events and today) — rules/underwriters judge continuance; tags describe. Reject per the fact-vs-conclusion rule

rejected.name: current_payment_status as enum
rejected.reason: kept as text (no enum coercer) rather than dropped

encoding_variations: Frequency: '$1,500/month', '$750 semi-monthly', '$346.15 weekly' — payment_frequency must travel beside ordered_amount or the annualized income is wrong by up to 4x
Support type: 'spousal support', 'alimony', 'maintenance', 'child support' are used interchangeably by different states but are NOT interchangeable for mortgage income — keep support_type verbatim
Governing amount: an original order plus a modification — order_or_agreement_date vs modification_date disambiguate which amount is current
Termination: stated as a fixed date ('through 06/2029') or as events ('until remarriage or death') — end_date_or_termination_events is a string to hold both forms

open_questions.q: No rule consumes this document today (Tier 3, rule_count 0). The field list is sized for a likely future income-continuity/receipt rule, not a known one
options: trim to the ~10 identity+amount fields until a rule exists
open_questions.recommendation: (b) keep the ~20-field income-analysis set so the rule can be built without re-extraction — this is the IH-1 lesson (a missing field kills the future rule)

open_questions.q: payment_history shape and length. Item count is uncertain (a verification letter may show 3 months or 24)
open_questions.recommendation: flat-row; revisit to per-field-wrapped only if a rule must attribute each row's source individually GEET'S DECISION (LP-438): BUILD IT — LP-437 made nested lists cheap (one declaration + the generic mechanism); the one-list-budget / defer / no-consumer concern is overturned. Build as flat_row; the per-rule consumer is separate follow-up.

open_questions.q: case_number appears twice — via the flattened court object and via account_case_reference_number
open_questions.recommendation: keep the court-object case_number and drop the generic reference field to avoid a duplicate

open_questions.q: support_type and current_payment_status are enums with no coercer
open_questions.recommendation: degrade to str and add a prompt hint listing the canonical values; add an enum coercer only if a rule needs to branch on them

notes: SPLIT from the former alimony_income_verification spec (LP-442, Geet's decision 1): this spec is ALIMONY / spousal support ONLY. Its continuance is the ORDER'S end date (end_date_or_termination_events) — alimony runs to the court order, per Priya. Child support is a SEPARATE spec (child_support_income) because it terminates at the child's emancipation age, a different continuance test.
Serves 0 rules today; the ~20-field income-analysis set is retained so a future income-continuity/receipt rule can be built without re-extraction (the IH-1 lesson).
PII: deposit_account_last4 needs _PII_FIELDS registration, pre_masked true. recipient_name / payer_name are standard-sensitivity names, acceptable as typed core, not registered.
Payment-history rows may carry an amount + account reference; the nested record needs its own redactor if any account digits appear (the transaction-description pattern).
Do NOT judge whether the income counts (a rule/underwriter call — tags describe, rules judge).
